---
name: implement-spec-with-review
description: Implement a high-level design and OpenSpec task specification through per-task management subagents and external Codex or Claude CLI sessions, with TDD evidence, bounded review and fallback, resumable logs, and final integration gates. Use for executing an existing implementation spec, not for inventing missing requirements.
---

# Implement spec with review

Use the Codex App agent as orchestrator. Each original task gets one Execution subagent and one Review subagent; they manage external CLI processes through `scripts/runner.py`. Keep those managers through fixes/fallback; create a new pair for the next task. Do not pretend Python can create App subagents. Do not have managers duplicate the CLI's full implementation/review. If subagents are unavailable, ask before substituting direct management.

## Before implementation

Read [workflow](references/workflow.md) and [CLI capabilities](references/cli-capabilities.md). Read every supplied original design, OpenSpec proposal/design/tasks/spec/scenario and diagram, check AGENTS.md and existing changes. Preserve original IDs and ordering. Build requirements → tasks → acceptance → named gates/tests mapping; record document hashes. Do not infer unclear diagram contents.

Every launch collect primary, reviewer and fallback **external CLI** model+effort independently; preserve settings supplied this time, and reuse previous settings only on explicit request. Run `scripts/probe.py` in the intended runner execution environment, including its required process-inspection check. Resolve authorized host-tool permissions as described in [CLI capabilities](references/cli-capabilities.md) before starting a provider. Probe actual local CLI version/help, capability metadata and authentication; verify IDs/efforts instead of translating App labels by guess. No silent model/effort downgrade. Three CLI settings do not select App or manager models.

Present one concrete plan covering mappings, order, gates, risks, exceptions, session/context strategy, finite budgets, baseline failures, log location and unresolved questions. Await user confirmation before implementation. Use [runner protocol](references/runner-protocol.md) to initialize the run and record the actual answer. A preflight policy is not implicit permission to resolve future uncertainties.

## Uncertainty and decisions

Read-only verification is allowed. Remaining ambiguity, missing information, conflicting specs or new authority must produce `NEEDS_USER_INPUT` with question, evidence, options/impacts and affected tasks. Orchestrator asks the user; pause affected work and dependencies. Runner saves the answer in decisions/discussion and includes it in subsequent CLI packets. Never substitute another reviewer's subjective vote for a user decision. Do not ask whether to continue after each task/round.

## Execute and verify

Use the approved runner protocol: bind real manager IDs, assess context, invoke CLI, run gates, review, and reconcile. Keep manager temporary inputs outside the candidate repository. Runner exclusively writes canonical logs. Saved independent reviews must be reconciled or explicitly invalidated through the runner before replacement. Agents may only provide structured results or isolated capture receipts. Fresh reviewer sees specs/current code first; runner saves independent findings before revealing the prior ledger. Round 1 fresh, round 2 resume, round 3 fresh; maximum five effective reviews. Round 2 incomplete gates require fallback for the next fix. High-risk tasks require an additional final-candidate independent review within the same cap. Read [review and recovery rules](references/review-recovery.md) before retries, rebuttals or session replacement.

For new behavior use TDD; consult the pinned [TDD adoption rules](references/tdd.md). Never delete existing user code to satisfy TDD. If implementation preceded tests, preserve it, add meaningful tests, label test-after truthfully and continue verification without asking solely about that deviation. Existing code is a valid starting point. Other ambiguities still require user input.

CLI success alone is not completion. Every task needs matching candidate/review/test evidence, acceptance coverage, no unresolved blocking findings or uncertainty, and all confirmed gates. A changed candidate invalidates related evidence. After all tasks, bind a fresh pair for `_final`, run full integration gates and a fresh selected-reviewer session. Final review has its own five-round cap and second-round fallback rule. When the fifth round blocks, save evidence and ask the user for the next step; do not raise the cap or create new tasks to reset exhausted budgets.

## Recovery and delivery

Resume only an explicit `.spec-runs/<run-id>` through `recover`. Never use last/latest session, concurrently resume one session, or rerun uncertain writes. Save checkpoints at each round/session replacement. Distinguish context occupancy from billed tokens; unknown stays unknown. Re-read original constraints and decisions after compaction. Logs are locally excluded from Git and excluded from snapshots.

Before declaring completion, run `status` and confirm tasks **and final gate** are VERIFIED. Report original IDs/status, changes, acceptance coverage, TDD/test-after and integration results, finding dispositions/rebuttals, decisions, fallback/context/session events, baseline exceptions, limitations, elapsed/available usage, and exact paths to `discussion.md`, `summary.md`, `decisions.md`, and the run directory. No implicit push/merge/deploy.

## Skill validation

Run `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v` from this skill directory. For isolated real validation use `scripts/make_fixture.py`; see [validation record](references/validation.md) for measured coverage and remaining provider limitations. The original requested rules and accepted amendments are retained in [requirements](references/user-requirements.txt) and [decisions](references/build-decisions.md).

# Adopted TDD rules

Pinned source: https://github.com/obra/superpowers/blob/5bf4e78011075bcfc0dc295f0724994cd123ee71/skills/test-driven-development/SKILL.md

Commit: `5bf4e78011075bcfc0dc295f0724994cd123ee71`
SHA-256 of fetched source: `64b03fce4aee5a97a93160cea8111f3ba13a17b7c001db4bd5836d67fd10705d`

Adopt behavior-first regression/acceptance tests, observed meaningful RED, minimal implementation, GREEN and optional refactor with full suite preserved. An import/syntax/environment error is not meaningful RED. Tests assert real observable behavior; mocks are reserved for unavoidable external boundaries such as deterministic fake CLI failures. Do not assert merely that a mock was called or that generated instruction wording matches.

User-approved precedence over upstream deletion rules: keep original code. Existing code is a valid modification baseline. If tests were added after implementation, explicitly record test-after and continue full verification; do not stop to ask solely about the process deviation, and do not pretend it was TDD. Never delete user code for compliance. New behavior should still follow test-first. Other genuine uncertainty is not waived.

Documentation/config/generated-code exceptions need initial user confirmation and an explicit alternative validation method. For building this skill, the user approved structural checks, realistic exercises and independent subagent evaluation for SKILL.md/prompts. Schema behavior still receives executable acceptance/rejection tests. All project tests must run at delivery; named baseline failures are disclosed and only specifically approved exceptions may pass. Do not weaken assertions, delete necessary tests, skip failures or silently substitute a single file for the full suite.

Before designing nontrivial tests, consult the pinned upstream companion writing-good-tests.md when relevant. If upstream guidance conflicts with these accepted user amendments, the amendments govern; unresolved new conflicts are questions for the user.

# Workflow and preflight contract

The immutable source requirements are `user-requirements.txt`; accepted build amendments are `build-decisions.md`. Do not weaken their quality gates for speed.

1. Obtain repository/workdir and original high-level design plus OpenSpec proposal/design/tasks/spec/scenarios. Read applicable AGENTS.md, dirty and untracked files, build/test configuration, diagrams and supporting documents. Record hashes and exact source paths in manifest. Parse Markdown task checkboxes with original IDs; where formatting is ambiguous ask rather than invent IDs. The runner accepts an explicit reviewed manifest, not an unreliable universal OpenSpec parser.
2. Create a mapping for each original task: requirement IDs, acceptance IDs, observable scenarios/tests, dependency IDs, original order, high-risk flag and named safe-argv gates. Expose oversized tasks, missing criteria, contradictory sources and changes to order/splitting for user confirmation. Do not rewrite source task checkboxes implicitly; state/manifest supply exact completion mapping.
3. Verify actual management subagent availability and two-manager lifecycle, CLI paths/versions/help, login, stdin/noninteractive support, explicit resume, output schema/events, sandbox permissions, required process inspection (`probe.py` runtime section), original document access and attachments. Validate the intended runner host-tool environment and pass that permission requirement to each management agent; use ordinary tool approval within existing authorization as specified in CLI capabilities. Display provider/model/effort/CLI/availability for all three roles. Model labels do not determine model IDs. Previous config is only a suggestion until the user explicitly reuses it.
4. Collect approved build/lint/typecheck/test/integration/e2e argv and measure baseline. No baseline failures are implicitly exempt; exceptions name task/gate and exact evidence fingerprint, with user authorization. If no separate lint/typecheck applies to a tiny fixture, disclose this; do not represent an absent tool as a passing check.
5. Ask all unresolved questions together. Record decisions and scope. Confirm role matrix, task scope/order, acceptance gates, risk, TDD exceptions, context/session policy, finite timeout/retries/calls/active time, baseline handling and log root before code changes. Defaults in make_fixture.py apply only to the already approved smoke fixture, never automatically to a real project.
6. Create a run with runner init, run baseline gates, then runner approve with the actual user's confirmation text. A supplied configuration is not confirmation. Managers are created in App and their actual identifiers registered with bind. Never fabricate manager IDs to get past a gate.
7. Execution manager invokes initial implementer, records full gates, then Review manager invokes fresh independent reviewer and reconciliation. Same managers and explicit CLI session resume continue fixes. Orchestrator reads compact status first and consults detailed evidence only when needed.
8. Finish current task before the next. If blocked, dependents cannot run. Independently runnable tasks may proceed only when the initial plan expressly permits it and independence is established. Next task uses new managers and sessions plus previous accepted dependency contracts.
9. After all tasks pass, execute `_final` full gates and fresh selected reviewer. Final integration review has its own five-round budget, fallback after round 2, and no artificial repair-task budget reset. All gates must pass before overall completion.

## Context decision before every call

Keep App, management-agent and external CLI context separate. Record source, reliable used/capacity if exposed (otherwise null), next-read byte count and action in context assessment. Byte counts describe planned inputs, not an asserted token occupancy. Never use lifetime billed tokens as current context. Consider space for tools/output and record the rationale in assessment. A configured `ask` policy pauses on unknown capacity. A user-confirmed `checkpoint-resume` policy permits continuation with unknown usage, while preserving checkpoints, limiting read sets to relevant originals, and using fresh sessions on insufficient capacity, observed compaction needing rebuilding, invalid session or unrecoverable resume. Unknown does not prove sufficient capacity. If the planned read set cannot be assessed within the approved strategy, ask.

Fresh sessions reread constraints, decisions, acceptance, unresolved findings and relevant originals. A manager replacement must provide a reason and checkpoint, not reset rounds/retries/time. Fresh independent reviewer packets omit prior ledger/status. Unresolved old issues are provided only after independent findings have been saved.

## Inputs and ownership

Canonical logs are only written by runner. CLI test capture writes invocation-local spool files; runner verifies/imports them. The runner does not require hidden reasoning: only observable messages, decisions, outputs and evidence. No secrets in prompts/logs. Known credential patterns are redacted; users must not provide secrets as source specs. Run directories are private local artifacts, not committed. `.git/info/exclude` is updated locally, including for shared worktree common Git directories; team `.gitignore` is untouched.

A plan to create an isolated project worktree requires user confirmation; use the App worktree tool and a fixed original-root run location. Current runner expects the repo used at init to remain available. It never deletes a user's worktree.

# Review, findings and bounded recovery

An effective round reviews a definite full candidate and returns a complete report. Independent phase and reconciliation together count once. Round 1 fresh; round 2 resume; round 3 fresh; rounds 4–5 resume unless approved context/session rules require fresh. Stop as soon as quality gates pass. Failed infrastructure attempts have finite retries and total budgets; they do not consume an effective review. Waiting for the user consumes neither reviews nor active execution time.

After round 2, unresolved blocking findings or failed completion gates select fallback for the NEXT correction. A new fallback CLI session stays under the same Execution manager. Ambiguity, environment and permissions are clarified rather than “solved” by a different model. Fallback role can use the same model/effort; disclose that only the session is fresh in that case.

High-risk task classification is user-confirmed. Such tasks need an additional fresh independent review of the final candidate, within five rounds. A suitable round 3 may satisfy it; round 1 alone never does. Reserve budget. Any later source change requires renewed relevant verification; never reuse a high-risk approval for a different snapshot. Fifth review must match latest code; failure stops, without another unreviewed fix.

Fresh reviewers first independently read original specs, acceptance, latest code, cumulative changes and interfaces. Prior finding conclusions/ledgers are withheld. Runner saves those findings, then phase 2 reconciles old ledger/rebuttals. An independent issue cannot silently disappear or be downgraded. Closed findings that reappear are reopened. Technical evidence may resolve an issue; subjective unresolved disagreements go to the user.

Ledger states: OPEN, ACCEPTED, FIXED_PENDING_VERIFICATION, VERIFIED_FIXED, REBUTTED_PENDING_ADJUDICATION, DISMISSED_WITH_EVIDENCE, BLOCKED. CLI reports ACCEPT/REBUT with evidence; completed ACCEPT changes go to FIXED_PENDING_VERIFICATION. Only reviewer evidence moves to VERIFIED_FIXED/DISMISSED_WITH_EVIDENCE. No new reviewer is introduced as an arbitration vote.

A source snapshot includes tracked, dirty, untracked nonignored files, deletions, modes and symlink metadata, excluding runtime logs. Ignored source inputs must be explicitly identified and included in preflight; generated caches are not code evidence. Submodules and unsafe symlink materialization are not guessed: unsupported layouts stop for a user-approved approach. HEAD alone is insufficient. Gate commands must not alter source; changed snapshots invalidate their results.

Authorized later tasks legitimately extend the repository. Earlier task evidence remains tied to its accepted checkpoint; final integration review examines all accumulated work. Unaccounted changes discovered on recovery invalidate prior completion and require inspection. Never use an old test/review to approve a changed candidate.

The event journal is authoritative; atomic state/checkpoints/logs are projections. Each invocation records its unique ID, task, role, provider/model/effort, session, worktree, process identity and snapshots. Repository writer locking covers all runs sharing a Git common directory. Reviewer workspaces are separate; the source is checked unchanged. Do not concurrently resume a session. If an old process is still alive, it must stop before write ownership is handed off.

For context pressure or manager replacement, checkpoint original document hashes, constraints, decisions, task acceptance, candidate, unresolved ledger, rebuttals/dispositions, failures, test environment/evidence and next step. Reload originals after compaction. Session replacement never resets budgets. Metrics unavailable from CLI remain null/unavailable, including precise read time, startup decomposition or context occupancy; do not infer them from billed tokens.

Foreground CLI and ordinary descendant process groups are terminated before releasing writer ownership. Detached daemon/service lifecycles are outside this runner protocol and must be explicitly planned in preflight; do not start them implicitly. Codex runs with its verified --no-daemon flag.
